VibePascal v58 -- x86_64-darwin native compiler (runs on Intel macOS).
A .ppu that is SHORTER than its own header declares is rejected instead of
silently accepted, and a half-written one no longer hangs the compiler forever.

Source commit:  dedf242c696a543f9626e2839ced40876478a98a  (dedf242c69)
Compiler fixes: c31227c8ca  (v57 -- a short read inside the .ppu reader is an error)
                dedf242c69  (v58 -- tppufile.readheader compares the declared
                             payload length against the physical one)
Parent release: v56 (a187bbac34).  This target SKIPPED v57, so it collects BOTH
                reader fixes at once.
Built: 2026-09-11, cross-built on x86_64-linux against MacOSX26.2.sdk (osxcross ld)
Binary: bin/ppcx64  size   9269256
                    md5    95ae70bde49d567e7b4c912eb7670e7a
                    sha256 9ab7be02558a2f6bbee5a243253d3cc236a73386dc55cb24a789946541b7a4fd

COMPILER BINARY ONLY.  Only compiler/entfile.pas and compiler/ppu.pas changed
between v56 and v58: no RTL change, no package change, and NO PPU FORMAT change
-- the reader got stricter, the format did not move -- so an existing v54/v55/v56
x86_64-darwin unit set stays valid and the utility binaries are unchanged and not
re-shipped.

WHAT CHANGED -- ONE ACCIDENT, TWO BYTES APART
  Both fixes are about the same thing happening to a unit file: a killed build, a
  full disk or an interrupted copy leaves a .ppu HALF WRITTEN.

  v57  A short read inside the .ppu reader is now an error.  Before it, a half-
       written unit could put the compiler into an infinite 99%-CPU spin with no
       message at all -- you had to notice a build that never ended and go looking.

  v58  v57 only ever noticed damage it happened to trip over.  Lose the TAIL of a
       unit and there is nothing to trip over, because nothing an interface load
       reads lives in the last handful of bytes: the compiler read what it wanted,
       never reached the missing part, and built your program against a unit that
       is not all there.  Exit 0, no message, nothing to search a log for.
       A .ppu header records how long the payload is, so a complete file is always
       40 bytes of header plus that number and can never be fewer.  readheader now
       compares the two and rejects a SHORT file.  Longer than declared stays
       legal, as it always was.  The arithmetic is 64-bit on purpose: the declared
       size is an unsigned 32-bit field, and a corrupt header claiming near 4 GB
       would wrap a 32-bit sum and switch the check off at exactly the moment it
       is needed.

  THIS DOES NOT TURN GOOD BUILDS RED.  The rejection is soft and self-healing: a
  truncated unit whose source is available is RECOMPILED and the build goes green;
  a good copy of the same unit in a later -Fu directory is used instead; only a
  truncated unit with no source and no other copy stops the compile, and it stops
  with the message an absent unit already gives.  Nobody is ever told to go and
  delete a file.

HOW FAR THE VERIFICATION GOES ON THIS TARGET -- READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING IT
  THIS BINARY HAS NEVER BEEN EXECUTED.  The build host is x86_64-linux, there is
  no macOS on it, and no packaged emulator on this box runs a Mach-O.  That was
  equally true of the v54, v55 and v56 binaries this one replaces; it is not a new
  gap, but it is a real one and nothing on this machine will close it.

  What IS established:

    - Format and architecture: Mach-O 64-bit x86_64 executable, flags
      NOUNDEFS/DYLDLINK/TWOLEVEL/PIE, checked with file(1) on the exact bytes in
      this tarball.

    - The build really recompiled the patched code, rather than relinking stale
      units.  compiler/x86_64/{bin,units} was wiped first; the build then compiled
      250 units, among them entfile and ppu, and both entfile.ppu and ppu.ppu were
      written fresh.  (A cross/native compiler build can return 0, emit a new md5
      and have recompiled a single file off week-old PPUs -- measured on this tree
      on 2026-09-11 -- so the unit COUNT is asserted here, never the hash.)

    - The fix is compiled in, by a SINGLE-AXIS Mach-O section triage.  The v56
      source commit and the v58 source commit were each cross-built HERE, TODAY,
      with the same host compiler, the same RTL units and the same flags, and only
      then compared:  __text 4382798 -> 4383694, a delta of 896 bytes.
      The control that makes that a source measurement and not build noise: the
      v56-source rebuild came out 9269216 bytes, the same size as the v56 binary
      shipped on 2026-09-10, differing from it in SEVENTEEN bytes of the whole
      9.2 MB file (the linker-generated LC_UUID), with every section size
      identical.  So the build is reproducible to within a UUID and the 896-byte
      delta is the fix.

    - The BEHAVIOUR of this source was proven by EXECUTION, on this host, against
      a control that fails.  The shipped Mach-O cannot run here, so the run used
      the x86_64-linux compiler built from the SAME commit, targeting darwin and
      reading real x86_64-darwin .ppu files:
        dist/ppu-truncation-check.sh <compiler> x86_64-darwin \
            packages/aspell/units/x86_64-darwin/aspelldyn.ppu \
            rtl/units/x86_64-darwin
      v58 source: 25/25 offsets clean, 0 problems, rc=0.
      v56 source (the preserved pre-fix compiler): 11/25, 14 problems, rc=1 --
      eight HANGs killed at 30 s, one silent kill, and five SILENT ACCEPTs of a
      truncated unit at 55293/55302/55308/55311/55312 bytes.  A gate that cannot
      fail proves nothing; this one demonstrably says NO.

  What is NOT established: that this binary starts, compiles or links on a Mac.
  If you have a macOS box, the one number worth sending back is the exit code of
  ./bin/ppcx64 -iV (expect 0, printing 3.3.1) -- it needs no SDK and no unit set.

AD-HOC SIGNING CHANGES THIS HASH -- A MISMATCH IS NOT CORRUPTION
  Every md5/sha256 above describes the binary AS STAGED, UNSIGNED.  Darwin
  packaging in Lazarus build-release.sh ad-hoc signs every bundled Mach-O with
  rcodesign, and the compiler is hard-linked into the .app, so the signature
  rewrites the top-level copy too.  A signature appends bytes and changes the
  hash, so the number above CANNOT match the file inside a Lazarus darwin tarball.

  Predicted AS-SHIPPED digests, if this binary is signed with no other mutation:
    ppcx64   9393168 bytes
      md5    3c4caf87a0167b016a615579aef40fe7
      sha256 7c868bbc14e7a6a469181b49f28d0c1dbf22860e492c6c39c61ccae267a2cef0

  These are a CROSS-CHECK, not the authority: build-release.sh stamps an
  "AS SHIPPED IN THIS TARBALL" block computed after packaging, and that block
  wins if the two disagree.  The prediction procedure was validated in the same
  run by re-deriving the v56 number: signing the v56 compiler under the name
  ppcx64 reproduces its documented 9393120 / 6e7a99a81afe9ec57ef133aad8da478e
  exactly.

  VERIFY UNDER THE REAL FILENAME OR THE NUMBER IS WRONG.  rcodesign takes the
  Mach-O binary identifier from the FILE'S NAME when none is embedded, and that
  identifier is covered by the signature -- so signing a copy called ppcx64.tmp
  yields a DIFFERENT hash than signing one called ppcx64.  The aarch64 binary is
  insensitive to this because its linker already embedded an identifier, which is
  why exactly half of any such check reproduces on the first try.
